verdict.rationale: Fern documents that it serves clean Markdown for any documentation page when `.md` or `.mdx` is appended to the URL. Its live llms.txt instructs agents to do this, and several `.md` URLs (sdks.md, cli.md, post/fern-agent.md) appear as working evidence sources. One probe returned a 404 at /learn.md, the docs root rather than a content page, which leaves 'every published page' slightly unproven but does not contradict the documented per-page capability. Missing for 10: independent corroboration that the `.md` variant works on customer-hosted sites, and confirmation that index/landing routes such as /learn also serve Markdown.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, every published page serves clean markdown at its URL (e.g. appending .md) so agents skip the HTML

citations.quote: Fern serves clean Markdown for any documentation page so agents can consume your content efficiently. Agents fetch the source by appending `.md` or `.mdx` to a page URL
For clean Markdown of any page, append `.md` to the page URL
